summary: Does a dying {Unstable} card enter the bin (and get trashed) before it is erased? The printed reminder and Caleb say it is erased in place of entering the bin. R137 (owner) says it enters the bin, is trashed there, and is then erased, and the engine does that.

sides.quote: (If they would enter a bin, erase them instead.)
"Unstable": "If an unstable card would enter a bin from an active

sides.source: R137 (its body-trash ruling and its Rector and Distiller notes)
sides.quote: Unstable units still die, they just get erased instead of ending up in the

sides.source: R137 (its body-trash ruling and its Rector and Distiller notes)
sides.quote: **An Unstable card that dies enters a bin, is trashed there, and is only then
therefore no trash". That reading is what the engine implemented until today,
Trashing means it goes to the BIN. But the unit that died was unstable, so
It's not a death, but it is a despawn and trashing. Weird corner case.

resolution: Settled by the authority order. The printed reminder ("If they would enter a bin, erase them instead") has one reading: the card never enters the bin, so it is not trashed. Caleb's "erased instead of ending up in the bin" fits it, R137 itself calls it "the plain sense of the text", and the owner's own words in R244 ("it didn't go to the bin") argue it too. Print and designer outrank R137, so zones.bin.unstable and keywords.actions.trash.unstable-death state that reading, and the exchange route follows (zones.changes.mods.exchanged says only that the unit and its mods are erased). The engine passes the card through the bin and trashes it: F-U07-6 (CT-246, filed as an owner decision on whether to change the engine). Register fix: mark R137's body-trash ruling, and R146/R152's trash on the exchange route, as outranked by the printed reminder.
